reason: E2 directly demonstrates that fast moving bed pyrolysis yields homogeneous NiPdPt alloy while slower heating causes phase segregation, supporting the core mechanistic contrast. E1 and E3 provide general context that thermal shock methods freeze high-entropy states and that slow kinetics cause segregation, but neither directly confirms the specific burst nucleation/supersaturation mechanism proposed.
premises: Ultrafast heating causes near-simultaneous decomposition of all noble metal precursors
Simultaneous decomposition creates high supersaturation of monomeric metal atoms
High supersaturation triggers burst nucleation that kinetically freezes a mixed alloy phase
Rapid cooling arrests atomic mobility to maintain homogeneous elemental distribution
Slower heating leads to sequential reduction and phase segregation
